# Complete angular leading-pole form and its conditional local estimate

The original round-pole action supports the angular extension of the
radial graph estimate. The proof retains every scalar Peter-Weyl degree;
it is not inferred from a finite harmonic screen or a chosen packet.
It supplies a local analytic estimate, not the dressed collider incidence,
a full Lorentz graph estimate, a physical boundary section, or an anomaly.

## Original operator and convention

`muon_full_d5_differential_form.py` retains the angular body

```
(i/R) [sum_a Gamma_a E_a - (3/2) Gamma_1 Gamma_2 Gamma_3].
```

`muon_intrinsic_scalar_discretization.py` fixes the right-frame convention
`E_a=2i J_a`, with `[E_a,E_b]=-2 epsilon_abc E_c`. Its normalized scalar
sections are `sqrt(n+1) conjugate(D^{n/2}_{mk})`. The m index is active
and the k index is a spectator of dimension n+1. The existing complete
degree reduction in `muon_chronological_spectral_blocks.py` confirms this
tensor identity. The `2*pi^2` unit-sphere volume is included once; it
multiplies both sides of the estimates below and does not change a gap.

The genuine pole germ has `C_rho rho/R -> 1`,
`C_rho h4=3/(2rho)+O(rho)` and `f_r cot(f)=1/rho+O(rho)`.
Retaining the eta term therefore gives

```
P0 = partial_rho - A_ang/rho,
A_ang = -I/2 + epsilon Gamma4 [sum_a Gamma_a E_a - 3 Gamma123/2].
```

This is the spatial normal/radial leading expression. Time derivatives,
the shift, lower-order gauge terms, and source/domain contacts remain in
the original equation. The pole is not the numerical strip face.

## Exact all-degree angular proof

Define `K=epsilon Gamma4 Gamma123` and
`S_a=i Gamma_b Gamma_c/2` for cyclic `(a,b,c)=(1,2,3)`.
The owned Clifford relations imply

```
K*=K, K^2=I, [K,S_a]=0,
[S_a,S_b]=i epsilon_abc S_c, sum S_a^2=3I/4,
epsilon Gamma4 Gamma_a=2i K S_a.
```

Thus, on degree n with angular spin `j=n/2`,

```
X=4 S.J,
A_ang=-I/2-K(X+3I/2),
X^2+2X=4 J^2=n(n+2)I.
```

The polynomial factorizes as `(X-nI)(X+(n+2)I)=0`. Equivalently,
spin addition gives `X=n` on spin `j+1/2` (multiplicity n+2) and
`X=-n-2` on spin `j-1/2` (multiplicity n, absent for n=0), in each
K eigenspace. Combining both K signs gives the spectrum

| Branch | A eigenvalues | Multiplicity of each before scalar spectator |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All n>=0 | n+1, -n-2 | n+2 |
| n>=1 | n, -n-1 | n |

These are two spin-addition branches of one harmonic representation.
They are not physical lepton families, selected modes, or occupations.
The original internal, physical-family, and conjugate copies retain
their own multiplicities. The proof applies separately to either collar
orientation and either owned Clifford representation.

The scalar matrix coefficients of all degrees form the complete
Peter-Weyl core on the inherited round `S3=SU2`. In the global right-frame
spin trivialization, tensoring that core with the original Spin4 and
internal fibers yields the complete angular spinor core. There is no
finite maximum n in this claim. Orthogonality and the direct-sum closure
extend the uniform estimate from that core to the domain of A_ang:

```
||(A_ang+I)v|| >= ||v||,
||(A_ang+I/2)v|| <= (3/2)||(A_ang+I)v||.
```

The second constant is sharp at the eigenvalue -2. The first constant
is 1, also attained there. On the positive spectral subspace alone the
first constant improves to 2, but a full regular solution can have
subleading components in the negative subspace. No such improvement
is assigned to the physical solution. Square-integrability of the
homogeneous leading powers excludes exponents <=-2 in the original
rho^3 density; it does not delete inhomogeneous or source-forced sectors.

## Radial form with angular coupling retained

For a compactly cut off regular core section u, using the cone comparison
measure `rho^3 d rho dVol_S3`, integration by parts gives

```
||P0 u||^2 = ||u_rho+u/rho||^2 + ||(A_ang+I)u/rho||^2
             - [rho^2 <u,(A_ang+I)u>]_boundary.
```

The boundary form vanishes for that core. Hence `||u/rho||<=||P0 u||`.
The fixed angular coefficient operator is self-adjoint on its stated
core/closure; no angular derivative was put equal to zero. For an actual
uncut section the boundary form must instead be retained. Multiplication
by a cutoff chi produces the actual additional term `chi_rho Psi` in
`P0(chi Psi)`; it cannot silently remove the physical outer datum.

The nonconical angular factor need not be bounded as an operator on bare
angular L2. Put `delta=rho C_rho/R-1`. The original spatial expression is

```
P = P0 - delta (A_ang+I/2)/rho + V0,
V0_scalar = [C_rho h4-f_r cot(f)-1/(2rho)] I,
```

with any other explicitly retained bounded spatial body terms included
in V0. The time/shift terms are not assigned to a bounded V0 without
proof. If the actual local domain supplies
`nu >= sup rho ||V0||` and `theta=(3/2)sup|delta|+nu<1`, then

```
||P0 u|| <= ||P u||/(1-theta).
```

This is relative form control of the angular term, not an assertion
that E_a is bounded. The regular germ gives delta=O(rho^2), but no cap
radius or numerical supremum is selected by that asymptotic statement.

For actual original-density comparisons

```
0<m <= C_rho R^3/rho^3 <= M,
|sin f| >= k rho > 0,
```

the useful conditional estimate is

```
||u/sin f||_(original) <= sqrt(M/m) ||P u||_(original) / [k(1-theta)].
```

It keeps the original geometric Riesz measure and eta profile. The
binary64 helper consumes explicit bounds and rejects theta>=1; it is
not an outward-rounded interval certificate, and none of m,M,k,theta
has been assigned as a physical input.

## Response and exact remaining scope

In the original common regular frame, regular background changes retain
the leading cone and eta coefficients, so `A_ang,Y=0`. If the frame or
domain is changed, its pullback connection must first be retained; this
is not a claim that every representation's raw coefficient derivative
vanishes. For a same-domain physical equation `P u=b` its response obeys
`P v=b_Y-P_Y u`. The inverse-profile source is

```
(u/sin f)_Y = [v-cot(f) f_Y u]/sin f.
```

Applying the estimate to the bracket additionally consumes its actual
commutator with P, the profile response, and all moving-density, frame,
cutoff and boundary contacts. They are not set to zero here. In
particular, angular variation of the profile response contributes
angular differentiation through the retained P. The leading common-frame
gap alone does not supply a total response norm.

The action still requires the actual incoming/initial fields, total

A0 = -I/2 - 3 epsilon Gamma4 Gamma123/2,
A0 = P_reg - 2 P_sing,
P0 = partial_rho - A0/rho.
```

The conical geometric contact contributes `3/(2 C0 rho)` and the
retained eta contributes `-1/(C0 rho)`. Including the round spin term
gives this A0, rather than the eta-deleted matrix. For a regular core
section `u=O(rho)` with a fixed smooth cutoff at the outer cap endpoint,
integration by parts gives the exact identity

```
||P0 u||^2_(rho^3)
 = ||u_rho + u/rho||^2_(rho^3)
   + ||(A0+I)u/rho||^2_(rho^3).
```

The first term is nonnegative and
`(A0+I)^2=4 P_reg+P_sing`. Therefore

```
||P0 u||_(rho^3) >= ||u/rho||_(rho^3).
```

The stronger factor 2 in this norm inequality requires `P_reg u=u`
throughout the support. Merely having the regular leading Frobenius
coefficient does not prove this: the physical remainder can mix the two
eigenspaces. The default estimate consequently uses factor 1. Without
the cutoff, the exact identity additionally has
`-[rho^2 u^dag(A0+I)u]` at the endpoints. A wall term cannot be discarded
by calling it a pole condition.

## Original density and a controlled remainder

The actual Cauchy density is

```
w = C_rho R^3 = rho^3 m(rho),  m(rho) -> C0^4,
|sin(f)|/rho -> |k| > 0.
```

On a specified regular cap, suppose the original profiles establish
`0<m_minus<=m<=m_plus` and `|sin(f)|>=kappa rho`. If
`P=P0+V`, `nu=ess sup rho ||V||<c`, with c=1 by default, then

```
||u/sin(f)||_w
 <= sqrt(m_plus/m_minus)/(kappa*(c-nu)) ||P u||_w.
```

Proof: the unweighted radial identity implies
`c||u/rho|| <= ||P0u|| <= ||Pu||+nu||u/rho||`; compare the same
original density on both sides. No renormalization occurs. The regular
owned expansions ensure that the comparison constants and a small
remainder exist locally when the stated real regular background is
supplied. This calculation does not assign their values or claim a
uniform physical cap/time interval.

## What the original equation must supply

Use the material-time split, avoiding an unnecessary inversion of the
shifted radial principal coefficient:

```
R4 = i epsilon Gamma4/C_rho,  T = i Gamma0/N,
D_t = partial_t-zeta partial_rho,
V = R4^-1 B0 + A0/rho,
D = R4(P0+V) + T D_t + sum U_a E_a.
```

Here B0 is the original body with the round spin, eta, geometry and
gauge contacts, excluding angular derivatives. The latter have coefficient
`1/R ~ 1/rho` and are not bounded multiplication remainders. Thus the
exact operand consumed by the radial estimate is

```
P u = R4^-1 D u - R4^-1 T D_t u - sum R4^-1 U_a E_a u.
```

The time and angular terms remain even on an exact solution `D u=0`.
Their possible cancellation prevents replacing this expression by the
Lorentz residual norm alone. For `u=chi Psi`, retain the shell source
`P u=chi P Psi+chi_prime Psi`.

The earlier causal-domain calculation also remains decisive: on the
saved near-wall finite slab, backward reach meets initial and incoming
faces, not the pole. This local cap estimate cannot replace those
physical data or realize the collider-to-Cauchy map by itself.

## Total source contact that must accompany the bound

At a fixed chart after the actual moving-domain pullback, the canonical
inverse-profile section is `v=sqrt(w) u/sin(f)`. Its independent source is

```
v_Y = sqrt(w)/sin(f) [u_Y+h_Y u],
h_Y = (C_Y/C+3 R_Y/R)/2 - cot(f) f_Y,
h_Y -> 2 C0_Y/C0 - k_Y/k.
```

The original pole owner has `A0_Y=0` under its regular variations.
If an actual common-chart source construction supplies `|h_Y|<=h_star`,
the unperturbed global radial gap gives

```
||v_Y||_(d rho)
 <= sqrt(m_plus/m_minus)/kappa
    [||P0 u_Y||_w + h_star ||P0 u||_w].
```

The differentiated physical equation must supply `P0 u_Y`, including
the full time, angular, coefficient, incidence and domain sources.
`canonical_inverse_profile_first` implements the exact density/profile
contact without conjugating an independent analytic first. A physical
real-path norm estimate and an independently ordered analytic contraction
remain different operations.

The smallest remaining operand for this route is now a specific
original-action radial form and its source, or a proved bound on the
displayed material-time/angular combination, on the actual dressed

## Action and density correspondence

The original `muon_full_d5_differential_form.py` has
`D_L,a = i Gamma_a G_Y/R` for the spatial hypercharge variation. Put
`w=C_rho R^3` in the original material/Haar measure, with
`Phi=sqrt(w) Psi` and the independent row
`ell=sqrt(w) barPsi Gamma0`. The ordered current in this canonical chart is

```
j_a^(D5) = ell [i (N/R) alpha_a G_Y] Phi,
alpha_a = Gamma0 Gamma_a.
```

The action-owned normalization of the physical left and right sections,
angular measure, normal mode and relative action units still belongs to
their common-domain construction. This formula supplies the D5 insertion,
not a numerical conversion of unnormalized sections into the complete
Maxwell source. No Maxwell kappa or extra self-dual multiplicity is appended.
The independent left field is never obtained by redaggering a source jet.

The original Maxwell coefficients, in precisely the same material chart,
have `e=h C_rho R/N`, `r=h N R/C_rho`, `d=h N C_rho/R`. Thus

```
c=N/R=sqrt(d/e),       n=N/C_rho=sqrt(r/e).
V_a = i alpha_a G_Y,
J_chi,a = integral ell [chi c V_a] Phi.
```

The common folded Maxwell density h cancels in these ratios. This is an
operator/coframe identity, not an identification of the Maxwell and matter
measures. Independent evaluation of N,R,C_rho from the original geometry
checks both ratios at the 49 saved nodes and the two transitions. The
ambient lapse is used; the induced wall proper lapse is not substituted.

For each of the 104 saved geometry/Higgs directions z,

```
c_z=(c/2)(d_z/d-e_z/e),
n_z=(n/2)(r_z/r-e_z/e),
(chi c)_z=chi_z c+chi c_z,
chi_z=B v_z,   v=K^-T w_wall.
```

At the moving roots, `rho_z=-p_z/p_rho` and the original coefficient and
basis radial derivatives are included once. Those readout derivatives are
stored separately from the fixed-rho PDE coefficients. No division by p
is used. The coframe remains nonnull at both stationary-coordinate roots.

## Exact normal-pair contraction and transport

The recovered normal-pair36 is `[W,JW]`, with `J=-Gamma0 Gamma_perp` and
literal dual `[D;DJ]`. It is not the older particle/antiparticle36
`[W,C W*]`. Recovery resolved this representation distinction before any

Gamma_heat = -(1/2) STr E1(c P_strat),
    P_strat = D_strat^dagger D_strat,
    c = i/r > 0,

with the original zero-mode/BRST quotient and relative zeta/eta completion.
The completion is not a second independent determinant. The owner module
`ae4_stratified_dirac_zeta_induced_owner.py` explicitly leaves the global
stratified operator/domain unrealized and prohibits setting the physical
cutoff to one. Here r=<psi,R_star psi>, i=<psi,I_star psi>; the surface Jacobi
term and bulk impedance both belong to R_star. No eigenline stationarity,
occupation or mode value is assigned.

The original two-collar law is interacting, not hard field continuity:
`muon_two_collar_weak_domain.py` supplies its right graph and independently
continued left graph and value/x/y/xy weak rows. The previously executed
projected-return report already exhibits a nonzero Higgs-seam Y commutator;
it is reused, not rerun. The finite squared/unsquared range contacts in
`muon_native_unsquared_domain_matching.py` are retained; a finite squared
inverse is not a substitute for the first-order physical complement.

The intrinsic native product uses L=W-z_cont Omega-i omega,
R=W+z_cont Omega+i omega. At z_cont=-i it is generally not Hermitian.
All trace statements below require the original same-domain analytic/relative
continuation, not a new conjugation of the right source. The full graded
trace remains distinct from the evaluated lepton18 coefficient component.
The conversion to the physical Lorentz/current functional, including lapse,
measure, state and domain correspondence, is still required.

## 1. New executed source coefficient

In the owned unit-S3 right-body frame the spatial principal of L is

    L^a = -i alpha^a/R4.

For a material temporal hypercharge test zeta(x), at fixed other fields,

    R_zeta = M_zeta U_R,  L_zeta = M_zeta U_L,
    U_R=z_cont G_Y/N_ind,  U_L=-z_cont G_Y/N_ind.

Differentiating P=LR on its factor core gives

    P_zeta = M_zeta U_L R + L M_zeta U_R,
    L M_zeta U_R = M_zeta L U_R + [L,M_zeta] U_R,
    coefficient_of(E_a zeta) = V^a=L^a U_R.                (1)

Derivatives of U_R stay in the zero-source-derivative part. This identity
does not license dropping the product domain contacts described below.

The new producer reads the saved 24 original matrices and theta22 directly;
no background/native campaign is rerun. Its last three matrices are
-i alpha^a, and temporal-Y matrix20 is -i G_Y. At z_cont=-i,

    V^a = -alpha^a G_Y/(R4 N_ind),
    G_Y = i diag(Delta I12, 2 Delta I6), Delta=sqrt(30)/20.

For *any* real unit material edge covector nu, Clifford and charge algebra
give

    V(nu)^dagger V(nu) = diag(Delta^2 I12,4 Delta^2 I6)/(R4 N_ind)^2. (2)

Thus the derivative coefficient has rank18, with singular values
Delta/(R4 N_ind) twelve times and 2 Delta/(R4 N_ind) six times. The saved
JSON records these actual coefficient values and matrix defects. No edge
direction, packet or state was selected. Equation (2) proves that the
vertex itself cannot eliminate the missing edge contraction. It does NOT
prove a nonzero supertrace, net edge charge or complete observable response.
The coefficient uses unit-S3 derivatives; the physical edge incidence and
surface density must still be pulled back from the same physical geometry.

## 2. The exact return contraction needed, not a diagonal-block heat

Reuse the proved full/complement identities. Write, on the actual pulled
domain, P=[[A,B],[C,D]], R_Q=(lambda-D)^-1,
M=lambda-A-B R_Q C, X=M^-1. The total logdet source is

    H_zeta=Tr[M^-1 M_zeta]-Tr[R_Q D_zeta].

For a derivative-of-test insertion V^a with four corresponding blocks,
cyclically collecting the actual ordered placements gives

    H_(d zeta) = -Tr[
      X V_A + R_Q C X V_B + X B R_Q V_C
      +(R_Q+R_Q C X B R_Q) V_D ].                           (3)

These weights are exactly the full resolvent blocks, including its returned
complement. The producer verifies (3) in a free noncommutative cyclic-word
algebra; no finite commuting block surrogate is used. It also verifies the
first and mixed differentiated identity with all ordered placements.

For f(lambda)=-(1/2)E1(c lambda), f'=exp(-c lambda)/(2 lambda).
On a justified common relative contour, the fixed-domain weak source is

    D Gamma_heat[zeta]=(1/2pi i) int_contour f'(lambda)
                                      STr[G(lambda) P_zeta] d lambda.

Consequently the derivative coefficient is the same contour applied to
the diagonal kernel of the four-block contraction in (3), with its minus
sign reversed. Its oriented boundary value is the candidate electric edge
coefficient before factor-domain, event and matching contacts. Equivalently
the local fixed-domain kernel is K_c=(1/2) P^-1 exp(-cP), whenever that
operator and its relative/zero-mode prescription are defined.

The actual uncomputed coefficient is therefore the same-domain edge trace
of K_c V^nu (or the equivalent full resolvent expression (3)), together with
the following product-domain contact. The existing regulated18 matrix and
its quadrature error do not evaluate this boundary kernel or its Sobolev
norm. Nor may the full heat be replaced by the sum of compressed heats.

## 3. Product-domain and event contacts cannot be inferred from the vertex

Let B_R and B_L be the original right and independent left factor boundary
rows, including their event, incidence and endpoint maps. The domain of
P=LR has BOTH conditions

    B_R psi=0,             B_L R psi=0.                    (4)

For the actual varied domain, its first source conditions are

    B_R psi_Y = -B_R,Y psi,
    B_L R psi_Y = -(B_L R_Y+B_L,Y R) psi.                  (5)

The second line is a concrete additional forcing of the left-factor
boundary row. It is not determined by the right vertex alone. At XY order,
differentiate B_L R psi as a three-factor product: nine ordered placements
occur, including B_L,XY, R_XY and both independent first-order products.
The producer verifies the full expression, without redaggering left data.
The same rule applies to B_R and to the moving readout/normalization.

The existing two-collar producer supplies local graph jets; its own scope
explicitly does not produce the physical event/outgoing jets. The endpoint
contact producer likewise preserves the normal-profile ratios, spin/gauge
transport and actual event source separately. Thus (5)'s full physical
left-domain forcing and the Green response to it remain uninstantiated on
the partial envelope. The source is not justified as a common-domain
bounded perturbation merely because the local 18 matrices are finite.

Artificial retained/released subdivision of one completed kernel has the
known opposite-normal cancellation. That old identity is not retested here
and does not supply the real branch/event contribution in (5). On the
actual edge the total coefficient must include the Green contact generated
by (5), any owned transition/corner return, and the relative completion.

## 4. Birth-cutoff edge term is explicit and cannot be assigned zero

Let q_i and q_r denote the edge coefficients of the complete test variations
D i[zeta] and D r[zeta], including their actual mode, domain and endpoint
responses. The owner does not make them independent free parameters. For
T=STr exp(-cP), the cutoff chain gives

    Gamma_c=T/(2c),
    q_c=(r q_i-i q_r)/r^2,
    Q_cutoff=(T/2)(q_i/i-q_r/r).                            (6)

This exact reduction is new to the electric edge test. r,i,T and their
total Y/XY jets remain symbolic, as do q_i,q_r. The generated expressions
retain their product and quotient derivatives. In particular, no mode
stationarity or uncomputed angular edge contraction is replaced by zero.
The known proper-frequency choice c=1 was a numerical coordinate for a
previous component, not the physical cutoff used in (6).

On one common source/domain ledger the necessary edge equation is

    Q_E = Q_fixed_heat + Q_factor_domain/event + Q_relative_log_eta
          + Q_cutoff - Q_owned_overlap = 0.                (7)

The terms partition the *one* matched functional and its variation; they
are not additional independently normalized loops. Local overlap is removed
once. Physical measure/lapse, source and normal motion belong to their
original terms. Total Y and XY derivatives of (7) must be taken before
using v30.1's moving-edge cancellation condition. Normalization of the
inherited boundary functional retains all nine branch/density placements.

No recovered identity evaluates the actual Q_factor_domain/event or
Q_relative_log_eta, or supplies q_i,q_r on this edge. Therefore this stage
does not prove either Q_E=0 or Q_E!=0. The missing coefficient is identified
by (3),(5),(6), rather than treated as a scalar zero or adjustable load.

## 1. Construct the actual finite-pair operator coefficient

The recovered four-mode occupation matrix is I4/2. The owned signed relative
one-body current coefficient, with positron normal ordering, is

    S=diag(1/2,1/2,-1/2,-1/2),  Tr S=0,  ||S||_1=2.

This is the exact bilinear coefficient of the already-adopted Fock16 pair.
It is not a replacement of its higher ordered products by Wick products.
The full exact pair density is preserved for those higher products.

On the *realized complete canonical Cauchy Hilbert space*, let the four
prescribed dressed columns form F:C4 -> H_C, F^dagger F=I4, including the
actual normal inclusion and density/frame isometry. Then

    Delta C_pair=F S F^dagger,
    ||Delta C_pair||_1=2,
    J_pair[chi]=Tr4(S F^dagger M_(chi V_phi) F).

The normal-pair form of this same insertion is v67's
Tr18[V_phi(C_ss+C_nn)]; both diagonal normal sections remain. The local
normal restriction is not by itself the complete Cauchy isometry F.

Since the exact transported V_phi is a negative projector, its norm is one.
For any bounded real scalar test chi in that common domain,

    |J_pair[chi]| <= 2 ||chi||_infinity.

This bound does not require the actual column values. It does require the
owned canonical normalization and a nonzero Higgs chart with unitary radial
gauge transport. No extra Maxwell kappa, V^-2 factor, spin average or family
multiplicity is appended. It uses the exact projector theorem, not the
slightly inexact floating U1 matrix as an exact projector.

In the original normalized-Haar scalar test basis, the addition kernels have
K_n(x,x)=(n+1)^2. For the retained n=1 and n=3 multiplets, sum_h Y_h(x)^2
is 4 and 16 respectively. Thus the Euclidean moment-vector enclosures are

    ||J_pair,n1||_2 <= 4,
    ||J_pair,n3||_2 <= 8,
    ||J_pair,n1+n3||_2 <= 2 sqrt(20) = 8.94427190999916.

These are conditional dimensionless bounds on the finite relative pair
block. They are not values of the physical charge moments, a physical
uncertainty, or bounds on the complete inherited/native/matched source.
Tr S=0 for the identity test does not imply vanishing weighted Q_H moments.
